ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: Without marks, or markless, is a phrase for being apart from marks, appearance, or form.
EvidenceBody: It is attested within 2,588 total occurrences across 324 allowlisted texts. Huineng's Platform Record gives a direct definition: "markless means being among marks while apart from marks" (無相者，於相而離相). It also says the teaching establishes "marklessness as its body" (無相為體, 11 occurrences). A later small assembly quotes that three-part formula and asks why marklessness is not also made the source. In a Compendium encounter, an unnamed questioner asks, "what is without marks?" and Layman Pangyun answers, "mountains green, waters verdant" (如何是無相；山青水綠). Transmission wording places "true form, markless" (實相無相, 103) between "the subtle mind of extinction" and "subtle correct teaching." The corpus further records Mazu Daoyi asking how to accord with "markless complete command" (無相三昧). These definitions, questions, compounds, and quotations keep the phrase tied to marks and their absence; this entry does not turn it into an imported theory.

ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: As a personal name, Wuxiang is the Yizhou master named in lineage headings.
EvidenceBody: The Linked Lamps lists "one lineage heir of Master Wuxiang of Yizhou" (益州無相禪師法嗣一人), namely Wuzhu of Baotang in the following text. Two independent lamp histories likewise place Baotang Wuzhu under this heading and say that Wuzhu first received the teaching from Master Wuxiang (初得法於無相大師). These occurrences name a person and must not be translated as the adjective "markless."
